OpsBot: INCIDENT ALERT: Prod-East 5xx spike detected — KV prefix cache growth + continuous-batching regression. Auto-escalation to P0. paging: @Ravi (oncall-sre)
Ravi (oncall-sre): acked. oncall jumping in. seeing a rapid increase in KV entries and CPU on prefix-cache-01/02. Requests per second steady but token processing latency spikes.
Maya (eng-runtime): looking at the aggregation window. suspect continuous-batching config change from last deploy rolled out 03:10 UTC. I see batch_window_ms increased from 8 -> 50 on canary. that could cause huge pending KV load + long-lived KV objects.
Luis (eng-ml): also seeing mismatched tokenizer hashes for several recent prefixes — a subset of prompts are regenerating keys repeatedly. combined with longer batching, we might be duplicating entries.
Ravi (oncall-sre): immediate mitigation plan: 1) roll back batch_window_ms to 8 on prod-east cascade. 2) force-evict prefix-cache TTL for high-card regions. 3) enable short-circuit fallback to stateless model for high-latency tails. prepping commands now.
Maya (eng-runtime): prepared hotfix config patch. snippet: ```yaml
# hotfix: revert batching window
continuous_batching:
  enabled: true
  batch_window_ms: 8
  max_tokens_per_batch: 4096
```
Ravi (oncall-sre): apply on prod-east pool (rolling) now: `kubectl -n inference set configmap runtime-config --from-file=hotfix.yaml`
DeployBot: Starting rolling config update on deployment/runtime-prod-east (12 pods). Canary -> 3 pods -> full.
Keven (cs): any visibility on affected customers? I'm seeing increased error rates for a handful of mid-market tenants (acct IDs: acct_08f3, acct_92b1). notifying acct owners.
Tara (product-ops): tagging as potentially customer-impacting. will prepare status doc. need rough ETA for rollback complete?
Maya (eng-runtime): can confirm canary updated, no crash loops so far. Applying to remaining pods.
Ravi (oncall-sre): canary done. rolling remainder. starting eviction task for keys with growth > 1M tokens. command: `curl -X POST https://cache-admin/prod-east/evict -d '{"threshold":1000000}'`
Luis (eng-ml): pushed tokenizer-hash-check patch to staging earlier but not prod. shouldn't block rollback. Followup: we'll schedule a postmortem for hash drift root cause (likely tokenizer version mismatch between model versions + template drift).
DeployBot: Rolling update completed successfully.
Ravi (oncall-sre): monitoring. latency tail dropping back to normal within 2 mins. 5xx rate falling.
OpsBot: Incident update: latency SLO breach reduced, 5xxs decreased from 7.2% -> 0.6%. continuing observation for 30m.
Keven (cs): off initial alert: two customers impacted briefly, no data loss reported. logged support tickets and informed exec contacts.
Tara (product-ops): action items: 1) schedule immediate revert PR audit to prevent future config flip. 2) enable automated pre-deploy smoke test for prefix-cache growth. 3) coordinate cross-team postmortem. assigning owners.
Maya (eng-runtime): followup hotfix to add guardrail in config loader: reject batch_window_ms > 20 for prod. will open PR.
Luis (eng-ml): will investigate tokenizer serialization differences. suspect a new tokenization patch on canary that didn't propagate to private images. prepping repro and evals.
Ravi (oncall-sre): handing off monitoring to daytime oncall @Maya in 15m. if we see any re-escalation, re-open this thread. Postmortem owner: Maya. Communication owner: Tara.
Keven (cs): will send customer-facing note once postmortem draft is ready. no immediate refunds; we'll wait on impact assessment.
Maya (eng-runtime): small note: discovered a metric anomaly — KV cache entry churn correlates with templates that include user-provided variables (template drift). adding an alert for unusual prefix churn.
OpsBot: Incident status: mitigated -> observing. next update in 30m or earlier if changes. :white_check_mark:
Ravi (oncall-sre): thanks team. handing off.
Maya (eng-runtime): handing off to daytime oncall. I'll follow up with a detailed postmortem timeline and root cause analysis (probable sequence: config change -> longer batching -> repeated tokenizer-hash mismatches -> prefix key regen -> cache blowup -> latency cliff).

Keven (cs): thanks, looping in affected account managers.
